messages:
alex (eng-infra): heads-up — several GPU jobs are Pending for ~10m, CA not scaling. pods show 0/8 nodes available: node(s) didn't match taint/toleration. I didn't touch any deployment yamls today.

mike (infra): which taint is reported? can you paste `kubectl get nodes --show-labels` and the pod describe events?

alex (eng-infra): pasted snippets below:
```
$ kubectl get nodes
NAME               STATUS   ROLES    AGE   VERSION   LABELS
gpu-node-17        Ready    <none>   2h    v1.26    pool=dedicated-gpu-v2,gpu=true
gpu-node-18        NotReady <none>   1h    v1.26    pool=dedicated-gpu-v2,gpu=true
worker-11          Ready    <none>   4d    v1.26    pool=general
```
Events from pod my-gpu-task-5 describe:
  Warning  FailedScheduling  30s   default-scheduler   0/8 nodes are available: 6 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate, 2 node(s) didn't match node affinity.
```
Also saw this on node bootstrap logs: `taint added: gpu-isolated=true:NoSchedule`
```

jen (sre): CI just applied a change to our launch templates this morning, added `gpu-isolated` taint so non-gpu workloads won't land. CA should still scale though — weird. any chance the pods used a different toleration key?

rahul (kube): quick suspicion: mismatch between taint key used by nodes and toleration key in podspecs. we had older tolerations like `key: redwood/gpu` in older jobs. can you grep podspecs?

alex (eng-infra): yep looks like older jobs have toleration `key: redwood/gpu effect: NoSchedule` while nodes use `gpu-isolated=true:NoSchedule`. so they don't match. example patch I tried locally to test:
```
kubectl patch deployment my-gpu-task -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"tolerations":[{"key":"gpu-isolated","operator":"Equal","value":"true","effect":"NoSchedule"}]}}}}'
```
Result: pod scheduled onto a new gpu node after patch. :tada:

mike (infra): OK that explains pods not scheduling, but why did CA not spin up nodes earlier? CA logs?

alex (eng-infra): CA event: `ScaleUp: No nodes are available that match pod's node selectors/affinity` and also: `ScaleUp: All potential nodes are tainted and pod does not tolerate key redwood/gpu`. weird because CA should be able to create nodes with our launch template that has taint.

ci-bot: deploy pipeline: commit 9f4c2ab — infra/launch-templates: add taint `gpu-isolated=true` to GPU LT. triggered at 2025-06-11T09:10:23Z

rahul (kube): probable timing issue: new ASG nodes get taint via user-data on boot, but CA considers node template *before* taint application when calculating scale-up. If CA thinks the pod requires a toleration it may ignore that template unless `--expenders` or `node-group` config allows. Also if pod has hard `requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` nodeAffinity that excludes the launch template labels, CA will not pick that group.

jen (sre): also saw a cascade: some deployments used `nodeAffinity requiredDuringScheduling` to pin `pool=dedicated-gpu-v1` which doesn't exist for v2 launch templates — those pods stayed Pending even after taint fix. we should avoid required affinity across rollout. convert to preferred with weight fallback.

alex (eng-infra): file a quick resumable fix: 1) add correct toleration to workloads 2) replace required nodeAffinity -> preferred during scheduling so CA can pick any gpu pool as fallback 3) ensure launch template applies taint early (cloud-init)

mike (infra): can we apply a temporary mutating patch to all GPU deployments? something quick: `kubectl -n ml get deploy -l workload=gpu -o name | xargs -n1 -I{} kubectl patch {} --type='json' -p '[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/tolerations/-","value":{"key":"gpu-isolated","operator":"Equal","value":"true","effect":"NoSchedule"}}]'`

alex (eng-infra): ran that on staging, looks good. prod I want approval but will do after we confirm no side-effects. one caveat: some job pods use `requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` for PCI-affinity (NUMA) and kubelet refused to evict them on drain — got a sticky behavior during node replacement.

rahul (kube): sticky eviction is expected if pod has `requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` — the scheduler won't move it, and `kubectl drain` respects `PodDisruptionBudget` + required affinity. to make scale-down/drain safer we recommend: use `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` for pool-level affinity, keep hard affinity only for hardware pinning that genuinely cannot move.

jen (sre): long term fixes: - update launch templates to set taint in the instance metadata at boot so CA sees it earlier - add automated migration job that converts required->preferred for legacy gpu workloads - add a prescale-check job in CA pipeline to verify toleration/affinity matrix before committing LT changes.

alex (eng-infra): thanks all. I'll open two tickets: one for quick toleration rollout (prod) and one for launch-template timing fix. will tag @mike and @jen.

mike (infra): ping me when you open the tickets. also add a small e2e that creates a GPU pod without toleration and ensures CA will still scale using our template (simulate tainted boot).

alex (eng-infra): will do. closing this thread for now — followups in the tickets. :thumbsup:
